title: A permissible blowup preserves the boundary and its strict exceptional part
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $H\subset B$ be a reduced union of irreducible components which is a strict normal crossings divisor; $H=\varnothing$ is allowed. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. Here a strict normal crossings divisor has regular irreducible components, and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular with every irreducible component of codimension $s$ in $X$. Let $M\subset B$ be a regular closed subscheme such that etale locally at each point of $M$, in parameters giving the above equation for $B$, its ideal is generated by a nonempty subset of those parameters. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], let $E=(b^{-1}M)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and put $B^+=(b^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $H^+=(b^{-1}(H\cup M))_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $X^+$ is regular, $B^+$ is a normal crossings divisor, and $H^+$ is a strict normal crossings divisor and a union of irreducible components of $B^+$. In particular $H^+$ has finitely many regular irreducible components and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular of codimension $s$ in $X^+$. As reduced closed subschemes, $B^+=B^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H^+=H^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$, where the superscript denotes strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform].

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

proof.text: The center has finite-type ideal because $X$ is Noetherian. The blowup is proper by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X^+$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finite component families for $H$ and for the closed subschemes of $X^+$. Away from $M$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] gives $X^+\setminus E\simeq X\setminus M$. Under this isomorphism [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-restrict] identifies each strict transform with its original boundary restricted to $X\setminus M$, compatibly with projection. All the asserted regularity and boundary properties on this open are therefore inherited from $X,B,H$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 4.1.2 and Remark 4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 hypotheses, printed p. 121

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-etale-charts] at every point of $E$. It gives actual etale lifts with regular local rings, distinct labelled hyperplanes for $E$ and the surviving $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$, and the reduced boundary equations, including strict-transform equations. At a point of $X^+\setminus E\simeq X\setminus M$ (step 1) take an etale chart of [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor] for $B$ at its image, restricted over $X\setminus M$, with $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$; as $H$ is a reduced union of components of $B$, its pullback is a sub-product $V(\prod_{i\in I}t_i)$, and [lem-trf-etale-component-coordinate-identification], applied to the regular components $H_a$, makes each $H_a$ through the point one distinct hyperplane $V(t_{i(a)})$ and the others empty there; $E$ is empty there and $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}=H_a\setminus M$ by step 1. These two kinds of charts supply the pointwise local hypotheses of the globalization lemma at every point of $X^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

proof.text: Discard empty $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$. Each remaining transform is irreducible: by [def-nagata-strict-transform] it is the closure of the nonempty irreducible open $H_a\setminus M$ under the complement isomorphism. Distinct transforms remain distinct there. The equations in step 2 and the unchanged complement from step 1 show that these closed subschemes are reduced. Apply [lem-trf-labelled-coordinate-boundary-globalization] to $Y=X^+$, $C=B^+$ and the labelled family $E,H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$. Its reduced union is $H^+$ by step 2 and the complement calculation. The lemma gives ambient regularity, normal crossings for $B^+$, and the finite regular components and all required intersections for $H^+$, as well as the union-of-components assertion.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

proof.text: On the charts of step 2, adjoining the exceptional hyperplane to the strict-transform hyperplanes gives exactly $B^+$ and $H^+$. On the complement the equalities follow from step 1. These are equalities of closed subschemes, since all the local ideals are the same products of distinct coordinate factors; thus $B^+=B^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H^+=H^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$. For $H=\varnothing$ the selected product is $1$, its strict transform is empty, and the same equations give $H^+=E$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

lean.statement: theorem permissible_boundary_preservation (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hX : IsRegularScheme X) (B H M : X.IdealSheafData) (hB : B.IsNormalCrossingsDivisor) (hH : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary H) (hHB : (H.support : Set X) ⊆ (B.support : Set X)) (hHcomponents : IsUnionOfIrreducibleComponents H B) (hM : IsPermissibleCenter B M) : IsRegularScheme M.blowup ∧ ((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical).IsNormalCrossingsDivisor ∧ IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical ∧ (((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical.support : Set M.blowup) ⊆ (((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical).support : Set M.blowup) ∧ IsUnionOfIrreducibleComponents ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical ((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical) ∧ (B.comap M.blowupMap).radical = strictTransformIdeal M B ⊓ (M.comap M.blowupMap).radical ∧ ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical = strictTransformIdeal M H ⊓ (M.comap M.blowupMap).radical
